item.title: Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps earlier records in its first EVTX chunk; carve it
item.description: Arctic Wolf incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log truncates the EVTX file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the record numbers, but the first chunk keeps its earlier records in its free space. On a domain controller the System log held 104 allocated events after the final clear, yet the encryptor's full command line, stamped about three hours before the clear, sat inside the allocated file, and Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM showed none of it; a PowerShell log in a second case held 44 records of which one was allocated.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB3

Cleared Windows event logs are not empty: Arctic Wolf shows that clearing an EVTX log truncates it after the first 64 KB cluster and leaves the earlier records in that chunk's free space, where standard forensic tools do not parse or flag them, and recovered a ransomware encryptor's command line this way

Arctic Wolf's incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log does not wipe the underlying EVTX file (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). On clearing, Windows truncates the file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the first and last record numbers, but that first chunk keeps its earlier records in free space until enough new events fill it (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). In a ransomware case the encryptor needed a password argument to run, and Arctic Wolf found its full command line inside the allocated System.EVTX of a domain controller, stamped about three hours before the final clear and absent from the parsed output of Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM; another log held a netscan execution record and an attacker hostname that survived the same way (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). In a second case a PowerShell log held 44 records of which one was allocated, all of them the same command that clears every log, which shows repeated clearing (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). Arctic Wolf identified no forensic tool that flags records left in the slack space after a clear, and records come back with some template-held fields missing (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).

Detection
The clearing itself is the alertable event, since Arctic Wolf notes that it often triggers EDR or IDS alerting and is frequently what exposes an attack in progress; the recovery step is forensic: when a log shows as cleared, acquire the EVTX file and carve its first chunk for records with earlier timestamps and lower record identifiers than the allocated ones (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Do not treat a cleared log as empty; preserve the EVTX files of affected hosts promptly, because new events overwrite the free space once they fill the first 64 KB, and search the whole file, not only the parsed events, for the encryptor's command line, tool names and hostnames (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).

item.title: Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind NtMonitor branding, new endpoints and an encrypted config
item.description: Rapid7 describes NtMonitor, a Windows build of SoftEther VPN Bridge 4.44 that it attributes with moderate confidence to Webworm, the China-aligned actor that ESET documented moving to European government targets in May 2026. The rebuild keeps SoftEther's function of bridging a remote network into the victim's LAN and strips its fingerprints: branding, handshake paths, the handshake watermark, the separate resource archive and the plain-text configuration are all changed, and Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability. Only one antivirus vendor detected the sample on VirusTotal although it has been public since January.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB3

Webworm's NtMonitor: Rapid7 finds a custom rebuild of the SoftEther VPN Bridge that removes the open-source tool's detection fingerprints (rebranded metadata, renamed handshake endpoints, a custom handshake watermark, an embedded resource archive and an encrypted configuration), attributed with moderate confidence to the China-aligned actor that targets European governments

Rapid7 analysed what it believes is a so-far unknown custom tool, a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge version 4.44 (build 9807) that it attributes to Webworm with moderate confidence (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Webworm is the China-aligned actor that ESET reported in May 2026 moving to European government targets and to dual-use tools such as SoftEther (ESET Research, 2026-05-20). The rebuild keeps the bridge function, which cascades a remote network into the victim's local network, and removes the fingerprints: the PE metadata and internal strings are rebranded as a network-monitoring product (inconsistently, since the service name and many registry paths still say SoftEther), the HTTP handshake endpoints get update-style names, the handshake watermark becomes a truncated PNG header so stock SoftEther peers cannot connect and the stock watermark cannot fingerprint the build, the resource archive that normally sits beside the executable is embedded in it as a PE resource, and the configuration is stored under a new name in a custom-encrypted format (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability, concludes the actor puts stealth above capability, and says only one antivirus vendor detected the sample although it has been public since January (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
Windows hosts in government networks that Webworm has already compromised; Rapid7 says that in every configuration it holds the VPN is set to bridge a remote network into the local one (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).
Detection
Rapid7's most reliable network detection, where TLS traffic can be inspected, is a POST request to an update-themed CGI path with a JPEG content type whose body starts with a PNG file header; on hosts, look for a SoftEther VPN Bridge service that was not installed by the organisation, in particular one whose binary carries its resource archive inside itself, and for firewall rules added by such a service (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Rapid7 calls the branding the easiest change for the actor to make next and says the endpoints and watermark can be swapped out trivially, so behaviour that is intrinsic to SoftEther matters more than any one string (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).
Defender takeaway
Government networks in Europe should treat any unmanaged SoftEther VPN Bridge, however it is named, as a persistence mechanism that bridges an outside network into theirs, and learn the tool's intrinsic behaviour, as Rapid7 recommends for the government sector (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).

item.title: Hokkaido: municipal data on a subcontractor's PC hit by K2F stealer via a game launcher; Rumoi's contract had ended
item.description: On 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 the Hokkaido municipalities Iwamizawa, Rumoi and Shintoku disclosed that data they gave their contractor GIS Hokkaido was stored on a development terminal of its subcontractor Rimgate that the K2F information stealer infected overnight on 2 to 3 November: up to 71,002 resident-register and 4,503 support-needed records for Rumoi, whose personal data was still on the terminal after its contract ended, 6,001 resident-register and 986 evacuation-support records for Shintoku, and fixed-asset-tax land and building data for Iwamizawa. GIS Hokkaido told ITmedia that the PC launcher of the game NIKKE is involved and would not say whether Rimgate staff ran the game on the work PC; no leak or misuse is confirmed, and none of the data contains the national My Number.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Hokkaido: resident-register, support-needed and tax data of the cities of Rumoi and Iwamizawa and the town of Shintoku sat on a subcontractor's development PC infected with the K2F information stealer, which GIS Hokkaido links to the NIKKE game launcher; Rumoi's data was still there after its contract ended

Three Hokkaido municipalities disclosed on 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 that personal data they had handed to their contractor GIS Hokkaido was stored on a development terminal of GIS Hokkaido's subcontractor Rimgate, on which traces of the information stealer K2F were found: the terminal was infected overnight on 2 to 3 November, Rimgate found the traces on 4 November and cut it from the network, and GIS Hokkaido told the municipalities between 13 and 16 November (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; Iwamizawa City, 2026-11-18; Shintoku Town, 2026-11-18). The data at risk is up to 71,002 resident-register records (as of February 2022) and 4,503 records of people needing support, with disability category and care level, for Rumoi, whose personal data was still on the terminal after its contract ended; 6,001 resident-register and 986 disaster-evacuation-support records for Shintoku; and up to 10,348 land parcels and 7,037 buildings of fixed-asset-tax data for Iwamizawa; none contains the national My Number and no leak or misuse is confirmed (translated from Japanese) (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; Iwamizawa City, 2026-11-18; Shintoku Town, 2026-11-18). GIS Hokkaido told ITmedia that the PC launcher of the game NIKKE is involved and declined to say whether Rimgate staff ran the game on the work PC; ITmedia adds that a third-party tampering with that launcher, which could deliver K2F on start, became public on 5 November (translated from Japanese) (ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19). This is municipal public-sector data held through a supplier chain.

Exposure
Any administration whose resident, social-care or tax data went to a contractor that subcontracts, and any supplier endpoint where consumer software such as a game launcher can run next to project data; the check is which supplier terminals still hold extracts from finished projects (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19).
Detection
The infection path is the observable: a consumer game launcher on a workstation that holds project data, and, because K2F steals passwords and allows remote control, password-store reads by non-browser processes and unexplained remote sessions on such machines; the sources give no more specific indicator (ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19).
Defender takeaway
Ask each supplier and its subcontractors which of your extracts they still hold, have them delete data of finished contracts and confirm it, and keep consumer software off the machines that handle it; Rumoi's contract had ended yet its data was still on the infected terminal (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19).

item.title: Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 cross-border work-permit records; no entry point or actor named
item.description: On 2026-11-20 the canton of Basel-Landschaft said that forensic analysis by external experts confirmed the attackers reached a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) and took data from it: about 97,000 records from applications lodged through its online platform since 2016-11-28, with names, addresses, birth dates, nationality, occupation, the ZEMIS identification number and employers' contact details. The canton cannot say which records left and assumes all did; it names no entry point, tool or actor, took the platform off the network and filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Canton Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 records from a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) in the cyberattack on the cantonal administration; the canton cannot say which records, assumes all, and names no entry point or actor

A confirmed data theft from a Swiss cantonal administration: the canton of Basel-Landschaft said on 2026-11-20 that forensic analysis showed the attackers reached a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) and took about 97,000 records for applications lodged through its online platform since 2016-11-28 (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20). It cannot establish which records were taken and assumes all, took the platform off the network, filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and names no entry point, tool or actor (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20; Polizeiticker, 2026-11-20), after other cantonal applications had been switched off earlier in the week (Inside IT, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
Persons for whom a permit-G application was lodged, renewed or changed through the cantonal platform since 2016-11-28, and the contact persons of their employers in the canton; the database kept completed procedures too, so people whose permits ended are affected as well (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20). The canton cannot exclude that uploaded documents such as contracts or ID copies were taken but has no indication of it (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
An online application platform that keeps every historic procedure puts the whole archive in play when it is reached, so check how much completed data your own citizen-facing and supplier-run platforms retain; employers of cross-border commuters in the canton should expect phishing and social engineering that quotes correct personal details, because the canton warns that such messages can be built from the stolen data (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20).

item.title: SAP Enterprise Portal JNDI injection from November 2025 is now on CISA KEV; confirm Security Note 3660969 is applied
item.description: CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties or a URL used in a JNDI lookup in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50) and read or modify server information; SAP rated it Medium, CVSS 3.1 6.5, and fixed it with Security Note 3660969 on its November 2025 Patch Day. No source names an actor, a victim or how it is chained.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2025-42884exploitedNATOA3

CVE-2025-42884, SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50: a JNDI injection that an unauthenticated attacker can use to read or change server information, fixed by SAP Security Note 3660969 in November 2025 and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CVSS 3.1 6.5)

CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, naming SAP NetWeaver, on evidence of active exploitation that it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-20). The flaw is a year old: SAP's November 2025 Patch Day lists a JNDI injection in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, EP-BASIS 7.50 and EP-RUNTIME 7.50, fixed by Security Note 3660969 at priority Medium and CVSS 6.5 (SAP, 2025-11-11). ENISA's record describes an unauthenticated attacker who injects JNDI environment properties or passes a URL used during a JNDI lookup, reaching an unintended JNDI provider, which could lead to disclosure or modification of information about the server, with no impact on availability, and it marks exploitation from 2026-11-20 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-20). No source names an actor, a victim or the way the flaw is chained.

Exposure
SAP NetWeaver AS Java with Enterprise Portal, components EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50; whether it is fixed depends on Security Note 3660969 being implemented, and the note text is behind SAP's login (SAP, 2025-11-11).
Detection
Web access logs of the portal for requests that carry JNDI environment properties or lookup URLs from unauthenticated sources, and outbound connections from the portal's server to hosts it does not normally contact, which a lookup to an attacker-chosen provider would produce; no source publishes an indicator or a post-compromise check (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Confirm Security Note 3660969 is implemented on every Enterprise Portal 7.50 system and apply it where it is not; the listing shows the year-old flaw is being used, though no source says against whom or with what effect (CISA, 2026-11-20).

item.title: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 6.1.6 or later
item.description: Apache's announcement of 2026-11-17 assigns CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) to Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, the same flaw it disclosed as CVE-2026-82384 for 6.1.5 in September: the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes vendor extension types before authenticating the requester, which gives an unauthenticated attacker code execution. Apache states the flaw is being actively exploited and CISA listed it on 2026-11-20, while neither describes the attacks; Roller 6.1.6 or later fixes it, and switching XML-RPC off in the administration interface does not help on older releases.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-129448 +1exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-129448, Apache Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5: an unauthenticated request to the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes attacker-controlled objects before authentication and runs code on the server; Apache says it is being exploited, CISA lists it, fixed in 6.1.6 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Apache's announcement of 2026-11-17 assigns CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) to Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 and says "This issue is being actively exploited" (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). It is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which Apache disclosed on 2026-09-25 for 6.1.5 only (Apache via oss-security, 2026-09-25). Roller's XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17); the servlet is mapped unconditionally, so the request is parsed even when the XML-RPC feature is switched off and no non-default configuration is needed (Apache via oss-security, 2026-09-25). CISA added CVE-2026-129448 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 (CISA, 2026-11-20), and Apache has not said who is exploiting it or how many servers are compromised (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-18). Roller 6.1.6 or later disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the feature is off, and the project's downloads page offers 6.1.7 as the best available release (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17; Apache Roller, 2026-11-21).

Exposure
Any Apache Roller from 4.0.0 to 6.1.5 whose /roller-services/xmlrpc path is reachable, including sites where XML-RPC was switched off in the administration interface; the checks are the deployed version and the enabledForExtensions setting in WEB-INF/web.xml, both of which Apache names (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). Roller is a niche Java group-blogging server with a much smaller market share than mainstream blogging platforms (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Web access and reverse-proxy logs for POST requests to /roller-services/xmlrpc from unfamiliar sources, and child processes started by the Java application server's account, since the flaw runs attacker-chosen code; Apache's announcement names no indicator and no post-compromise check, and an upgrade does not undo an earlier compromise (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later now; where that waits, Apache's interim steps are setting enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or removing the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restarting (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). Treat an exposed instance on an older release as possibly compromised, because Apache and CISA report exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-20).

item.title: Update: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
item.description: Danfoss published CVE ids for two controller flaws: CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in a coming 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, documented default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix). BSI's version 1.1 warning reports exploitation attempts against two Copeland XWEB EVO flaws.
item.content:encoded:
Update21 Nov 2026 04:39 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-intelsummarytechniquescvessourcesevidencebody

Danfoss published CVE ids for two controller flaws: CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in a coming 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, documented default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix). BSI's version 1.1 warning reports exploitation attempts against two Copeland XWEB EVO flaws.

Danfoss published two advisories on 2026-11-20. DSA-2026-12-01 assigns CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3) to a stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler of the AK-SM 8xxA series, firmware 5.4.0 and earlier: crafted HTTP or HTTPS POST requests cause memory corruption and a web-server restart and, in Danfoss's words, hypothetically arbitrary code execution with web-server privileges, with no authentication; the fix is an announced 5.5.x release that is not yet published, Danfoss will remove the option to disable Strict mode, and its mitigations are no internet exposure, access only through a VPN or protected network, Strict mode and strong passwords (Danfoss, 2026-11-20). DSA-2026-12-02 assigns CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9) to default or known passwords on all versions of the legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, which shipped with default credentials documented in the product manual; Danfoss's remediation is to replace the fleet with the AK-SM 800A series (Danfoss, 2026-11-20). Neither advisory reports exploitation in the wild or says whether CVE-2026-129713 is one of the six flaws Midnight Blue reported. BSI's warning, now at version 1.1 (2026-11-17), reports sensor-observed exploitation attempts against two Copeland XWEB EVO flaws (translated from German) (BSI, 2026-11-17).

Open finding: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised in France, six more European countries and Switzerland, with France blaming the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh for the October campaign; Midnight Blue reports six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2 →

item.title: Update: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
item.description: Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual as affected with no fix, and Cisco's advisory version 1.3 moves Catalyst Center to not affected and shows IOS XE, ISE and UCS Central as not affected, so the earlier Cisco listing of Catalyst Center as affected no longer holds.
item.content:encoded:
Update21 Nov 2026 04:38 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiescvessourcesevidencebody

Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual as affected with no fix, and Cisco's advisory version 1.3 moves Catalyst Center to not affected and shows IOS XE, ISE and UCS Central as not affected, so the earlier Cisco listing of Catalyst Center as affected no longer holds.

Cisco's advisory is now at version 1.3 (2026-11-20), whose change log reads "Changed Catalyst Center from affected to not affected", and its product table shows Catalyst Center, IOS XE, ISE and UCS Central as not affected, so the Cisco product list above follows that version (Cisco, 2026-11-20). Siemens has published two advisories for CVE-2026-114938 and lists no fix for either: Siveillance Control and Siveillance Control Pro, the physical-security management systems, with the JVM option -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics on the client until Java is updated (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-19), and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual, where Siemens' immediate measure is to block direct internet access or shut the instances down (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-18). Neither Cisco nor Siemens reports exploitation of its products.

Open finding: Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later and Oracle Java SE on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI: a heap overflow in the Base64 decoder that its discoverer chains into pre-authentication code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; fixed in 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts, none confirmed successful against its sensors (CVSS 3.1 8.1) →

item.title: Update: NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update 1.31.9, 1.30.7 or Plus 37.3.0.1
item.description: Four vendors published product impact for the nginx flaws: Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled (three fixed builds out, three due 2026-11-23, HTTP/2 off as workaround), Cisco lists NX-OS and ISE 3.5 among affected products, Siemens Industrial Edge has no fix, and Fortinet is still investigating. None reports exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
Update21 Nov 2026 04:37 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiessourcesevidenceactionsbody

Four vendors published product impact for the nginx flaws: Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled (three fixed builds out, three due 2026-11-23, HTTP/2 off as workaround), Cisco lists NX-OS and ISE 3.5 among affected products, Siemens Industrial Edge has no fix, and Fortinet is still investigating. None reports exploitation.

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama (virtual and M-Series) as affected by CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 only where the HTTP/2 option is enabled, and says it knows of no malicious exploitation; disabling HTTP/2 is its workaround (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-11-20). The fixed builds are PAN-OS 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6 and 11.2.16-h3; 12.1.7-h15, 11.2.10-h19 and 11.2.13-h6 carry an ETA of 2026-11-23, and 12.1.2 to 12.1.4 and 11.2.0 to 11.2.7 need no action (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-11-20).

Cisco's interim advisory (version 1.0, 2026-11-20) lists NX-OS Software, Smart PHY (fix 27.1.0, March 2027), the Intersight Virtual Appliance (1.1.9-0, December 2026), Cloud Hosted Services Vulnerability Management (1.30.7, November 2026) and Identity Services Engine 3.5 (3.5 Patch 5, December 2026) as affected, lists Catalyst Center, the SD-WAN Controller and Manager, ASA, FMC, FTD and UCS Central as not affected, and has IOS XE, IOS XR and UCS Director under investigation; its PSIRT knows of proof-of-concept code and of no malicious use (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Siemens (SSA-935812, 2026-11-20) lists Industrial Edge products as affected in all versions with no fix available and names disabling HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 on the affected listeners as the mitigation (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-20). Fortinet says none of its products uses NGINX Plus and is still investigating FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and dozens of others (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20).

Open finding: NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated memory-corruption flaws (CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 in HTTP/2, CVE-2026-121810 in HTTP/3, CVE-2026-123634 in the resolver, CVE-2026-113425 in the mail proxy) can lead to code execution as the worker process; fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, Rapid7 proof of concept public, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.2) →

item.title: Update: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
item.description: CISA listed CVE-2026-76466 as exploited on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that soon after a public proof of concept appeared attackers compromised two internet-reachable Expressway X15.5.3 devices, then two internal cluster nodes, with root used for scanning and credential theft; Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. Priority moves to high.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Update: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
item.description: Elastic confirms Elasticsearch 7.17.3 and later is affected, with remote code execution needing an authenticated read-level user and unauthenticated actors limited to denial of service, and announces fixes without dates; Broadcom lists released Tanzu fixes and Palo Alto Networks lists fixed builds, none reporting exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
Update20 Nov 2026 05:12 UTCrun 2026-11-20T0356Z-intelentitiesaffected_productssourcesbodysummarycves

Elastic confirms Elasticsearch 7.17.3 and later is affected, with remote code execution needing an authenticated read-level user and unauthenticated actors limited to denial of service, and announces fixes without dates; Broadcom lists released Tanzu fixes and Palo Alto Networks lists fixed builds, none reporting exploitation.

Three more vendors published product status. Elastic says Elasticsearch 7.17.3 and later is affected with mitigating factors: remote code execution needs an authenticated user with at least read access on an affected CPU architecture, while unauthenticated actors can cause denial of service; Logstash 8.6.2 and later is affected only through the elastic_integration filter when an ingest pipeline decodes Base64 from an untrusted source, with a crash as the result, and Kibana, Beats, Elastic Agent, APM Server, the ECK operator and Elastic Maps Server are not affected, while Elasticsearch clusters that ECK manages follow the Elasticsearch rule (Elastic, 2026-11-19). Elastic plans fixes in 8.19.26, 9.4.10, 9.5.7 and 9.6.0 with a bundled JDK 27.0.1.1+4 and gives no dates, hot-fixed Elastic Cloud Serverless on 2026-11-18, and says fewer than about 5% of Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, on Azure only, run an affected CPU architecture; a self-managed node is affected only on an x86-64 CPU with AVX512_VBMI (Elastic, 2026-11-19).

Broadcom's Tanzu advisory TNZ-2026-1107 says several Tanzu products ship affected Java runtimes and lists released fixes: Java Buildpack 5.5.0 and 5.5.1, Ruby Buildpack 1.10.104, Tanzu OpenJDK 17.0.21.1+5, 21.0.13.1+5 and 25.0.5.1+5 and Foundation Core 3.1.19, 3.3.10 and 11.0.3, where the identity service and CredHub carry an affected Java 25 runtime that Tanzu has not yet confirmed from the bill of materials; it names -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as the preferred workaround (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). Palo Alto Networks lists fixed builds of Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector and the Secure Access HTML5 Gateway, says PAN-OS is not affected, offers no workaround and is not aware of any malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-20). None of these statuses changes the exploitation picture above.

Open finding: Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later and Oracle Java SE on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI: a heap overflow in the Base64 decoder that its discoverer chains into pre-authentication code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; fixed in 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts, none confirmed successful against its sensors (CVSS 3.1 8.1) →

item.description: The same advisory fixed CVE-2026-115732 (CVSS 4.0 9.0), a certificate-name authorization bypass that lets a certificate for a name extending a real host name authenticate as that host; the fixed builds are the same and Puppet Core 9.1.3 and 8.22.2 are added. CISA lists only CVE-2026-115731, and exploitation of the second flaw is not established.
item.content:encoded:
Improvement20 Nov 2026 05:12 UTCrun 2026-11-20T0356Z-intelsummaryaffected_productscvessourcesactionsbodyentities

The same advisory fixed CVE-2026-115732 (CVSS 4.0 9.0), a certificate-name authorization bypass that lets a certificate for a name extending a real host name authenticate as that host; the fixed builds are the same and Puppet Core 9.1.3 and 8.22.2 are added. CISA lists only CVE-2026-115731, and exploitation of the second flaw is not established.

The same Perforce advisory fixed a second flaw, CVE-2026-115732, an authorization bypass in the certificate-name matching of Puppet's authorization library, scored CVSS 4.0 9.0: a CA-signed certificate whose name extends or shortens an authorised host name is authorised as that host (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03). Neodyme's example is that an attacker who got a certificate for evil.target.lab.local can authenticate as target.lab.local, then fetch that host's catalog, which can carry configuration files with database credentials and API tokens, push spoofed facts and add exported resources (Neodyme, 2026-11-03). Where the CA autosigns, such a certificate can be requested for a name that does not exist yet, and OpenVox says autosign is not the default but is common in real deployments (OpenVox, 2026-11-03); NCSC.ch adds that in Puppet Enterprise the bypass also enables CA administration and remote command execution on managed nodes (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

The fix is in the same Puppet Enterprise builds, in Puppet Core 9.1.3 and 8.22.2 and, for OpenVox Server and OpenVoxDB, in 9.2.0 and 8.18.0 (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-18; OpenVox, 2026-11-03). CISA's catalog entry covers only CVE-2026-115731 (CISA, 2026-11-17); NCSC.ch labels the pair actively exploited with a proof of concept available and lists a community report as an additional source (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19), while the report The Hacker News quotes describes a CVE-2026-115731 intrusion, so exploitation of CVE-2026-115732 itself is not established (The Hacker News, 2026-11-18). NCSC.ch's temporary measures are to disable certificate autosigning, enforce strong request validation, audit the issued certificates for colliding names and review the CA configuration for signs of compromise (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

Open finding: CVE-2026-115731, Puppet Enterprise before 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1: deserialization of a crafted agent report gives code execution as the Puppet service user to any holder of a CA-signed agent certificate, and unauthenticated where the CA autosigns; CISA lists it as exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.4) →

Università della Svizzera italiana (USI, Lugano): third parties exploited a vulnerability in an online-forms system and had access to form responses and attached documents from 9 to 17 November 2026, mainly contact details, and more than 8,000 e-mails warned those concerned; USI names no product or actor

USI said on 2026-11-19 that unauthorised third parties had access to data held on one of its applications between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17, by exploiting a vulnerability in the software of an online-forms system that the university uses to collect certain job applications, scholarship requests and surveys (USI via Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-19). Defender takeaway
Check any forms, survey or application-intake system, your own or a supplier's, that stores uploaded documents, and treat those documents as exposed on a system that was reachable with vulnerable software during the access window of 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-17 (USI via laRegione, 2026-11-19).

item.title: Mitel OpenScape 4000: two unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Platform flaws; upgrade to V11 R2.14 or restrict access
item.description: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager: an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw and an unauthenticated command injection, both CVSS 3.1 10.0, and a command injection reachable from the adjacent network (9.6). CVE ids have been requested but not assigned; the fix is V11 R2.14, PLT HF5 on V11 R1.26 or a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, and enabling Security Mode restricted access is Mitel's workaround. item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

Mitel OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, MISA-2026-0013: two unauthenticated flaws in the Platform component rated CVSS 3.1 10.0 (improper authentication, command injection) and an adjacent-network command injection (9.6); CVE ids pending, fixed in V11 R2.14, Security Mode restricted access is the workaround, no exploitation stated

Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, tracked by Mitel's internal ids because the CVE identifiers it requested are not yet assigned (Mitel, 2026-11-18). MTLVULN-1785 is an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw that gives unauthorized access and MTLVULN-1786 an unauthenticated command injection through insufficient parameter sanitization, both CVSS 3.1 10.0 with changed scope; MTLVULN-1793 is a command injection that an unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access can use, scored 9.6 (Mitel, 2026-11-18). Affected are OpenScape 4000 V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.68 and earlier, and OpenScape 4000 Manager V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.34, R1.42, R1.54 and R1.68; Mitel does not assess end-of-support releases (Mitel, 2026-11-18).

The issues are corrected in V11 R2.14, Mitel provides PLT HF5 for V11 R1.26 and a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22 (for the Manager, V10 R1.34 to V11 R0.22), and for customers who cannot apply the fix quickly, enabling Security Mode restricted access is a workaround that prevents exploitation, with the steps in a portal-only article (Mitel, 2026-11-18). CERT-FR lists the risks as remote arbitrary code execution, remote denial of service, policy bypass and loss of integrity and confidentiality, and BSI describes an attacker who can bypass safeguards, disclose information or run arbitrary commands in the context of the system (CERT-FR, 2026-11-19; BSI, 2026-11-19). Mitel's text does not mention exploitation.

Exposure
OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager at the releases above; the vulnerable component is the Platform, and the advisory does not say which of its interfaces are normally reachable (Mitel, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Unauthenticated access to the Platform component from hosts that are not administration or maintenance systems, and unexpected command execution on the platform; both follow from the improper-authentication and command-injection mechanisms, and the advisory gives no detection guidance.
Defender takeaway
Apply the fix for the release in use now; where that waits, turn on Security Mode restricted access, and read the affected range against CERT-FR's wording if the system runs R2.12 or R2.13 (Mitel, 2026-11-18; CERT-FR, 2026-11-19).

item.title: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14 fix seven memory flaws; a Rails exploit is announced for 25 November: update the interpreter
item.description: The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. Veria Labs, which found the case-conversion flaw independently (CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte heap overflow), says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed without authentication in their default configuration and plans to publish a code-execution proof of concept on stock Rails on 25 November 2026; no exploitation is reported. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life, and the interpreter itself, not a gem, must be updated.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-132825NATOA2

Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14: seven memory-safety flaws in the regexp engine and string case conversion, three rated Critical by the project, with proofs of concept for code execution; Veria Labs says Rails and classic Sinatra are exposed by default and announces a public Rails exploit for 25 November 2026 (CVE-2026-132825, CVSS 3.1 7.4)

The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 to fix seven vulnerabilities in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, and says it is aware of proofs of concept that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution (Ruby project, 2026-11-18). NCSC.ch lists three as Critical, a one-byte heap overflow in case conversion of strings in single-byte encodings such as ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252, a double free in regexp compilation and a heap overflow from an integer overflow in regexp compilation, and the rest as High or Moderate (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19); the project's advisory for the first confirms it can write one byte past the output buffer (Ruby project, 2026-11-18). Most regexp flaws need an application that compiles, matches or stringifies an attacker-controlled pattern, and one needs only a crafted subject string against a fixed case-insensitive backreference pattern; the case-conversion flaw needs attacker-controlled text passed to a case-changing method (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19). Affected are Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 to 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 to 4.0.9, and Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life and unfixed (Ruby project, 2026-11-18).

NCSC.ch and watchTowr say Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed to the case-conversion overflow in their default configuration, and watchTowr reports no exploitation as of 2026-11-19 (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19; watchTowr, 2026-11-19). Veria Labs, which says it found the flaw independently and first demonstrated code execution, calls it Ruby2Shell, says it is reachable without authentication on Rails and classic Sinatra and that plain Rack and other frameworks are not exposed by default, and plans to publish a proof of concept for remote code execution on stock Rails on 25 November 2026, or later if major vendors have not shipped a fix (Veria Labs, 2026-11-20). Veria lists GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22.5 and earlier and Chatwoot 4.20.0 and earlier as having no fixed release, and GitLab (fixed in 19.6.1, 19.5.8 and 19.4.10), Mastodon, OpenProject and the Discourse base image as patched; the Ruby advisories name no product, so the vendors' own advisories decide for each (Veria Labs, 2026-11-20). CVE-2026-132825 names the case-conversion overflow and is scored CVSS 3.1 7.4 with a local attack vector and high complexity (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-19); the Ruby announcement says CVE identifiers were requested and none was assigned at publication, so the other six flaws are known by GHSA id (Ruby project, 2026-11-18).

Exposure
Ruby 3.3, 3.4 and 4.0 below the fixed releases that run Rails or classic Sinatra, or any application that passes untrusted text to a case-changing method or compiles untrusted regexp patterns; the interpreter version is shown by ruby -v, and self-hosted products that bundle Ruby carry their own fix timeline (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).
Detection
Crashes, segmentation faults and abnormal restarts of Ruby application workers that coincide with requests carrying long single-byte-encoded text or unusual regexp parameters, and a shell or network tool spawned by a Ruby worker process; these follow from the memory-corruption mechanism, as no source gives detection guidance.
Defender takeaway
Update the interpreter, not the gems, rebuild container images and restart workers before the announced proof of concept; until then NCSC.ch's temporary measures are to avoid compiling regexps from untrusted input and, for the case-conversion flaw, to convert input to UTF-8 so the vulnerable path is not reached (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

item.title: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36: FPM request smuggling to code execution; the open session flaw is fixed
item.description: The PHP project released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19 with fixes for up to 18 CVEs per branch. The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM keeps unread php://input bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so an unauthenticated multipart request can plant a second FastCGI request and run PHP code as the worker, but only behind a front end that reuses FastCGI connections, which standard nginx and Apache setups do not. The release also fixes CVE-2026-115560, left open in October, and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix; no source reports exploitation or a public proof of concept.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-129289 +7NATOA2

PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36: CVE-2026-129289 lets an unauthenticated request smuggle a second FastCGI request into PHP-FPM and run PHP code when the front end reuses FastCGI connections; the release also fixes the session flaw left open in October and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

The PHP project released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19, and the changelogs list up to 18 CVEs per branch (PHP, 2026-11-19). The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: when php://input was opened but not read to the end, PHP-FPM leaves the unread request bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so a malformed multipart body can place a second FastCGI request inside the first, and an unauthenticated attacker can bypass front-end routing and execute attacker-controlled PHP code with the privileges of the worker (PHP, 2026-11-19). It requires a front end that enables persistent backend connections and an application path that opens php://input without reading it fully; standard nginx and Apache configurations that close the FastCGI connection after each request are not affected by the demonstrated attack (PHP, 2026-11-19).

Two session flaws close the item the October release left open (watchTowr, 2026-11-20): CVE-2026-115560, where upload-progress session data is written in one serializer format and read in another, and CVE-2026-126714, where an interrupted write by the default files handler leaves a mixed old and new session file; both end in object injection and need an object gadget chain in the application (PHP, 2026-11-19; PHP, 2026-11-19). The fix for the first disables upload progress by default (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129481, a use-after-free of a stale session filename after an interrupted session shutdown, is in PHP's words an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619 and affects PHP 8.3 and later, and CVE-2026-129182, for PHP 8.5 only, covers further scenarios after the 8.5.12 fix (PHP, 2026-11-19; PHP, 2026-11-19).

CVE-2026-129474, PHP 8.5 only, is exposed on the built-in defaults, because fatal error backtraces are on in 8.5 and the default includes arguments, and php.ini-production, which sets zend.exception_ignore_args=1, or fatal_error_backtraces=0 prevents the attack; PHP confirmed code execution on 8.5 (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129496 needs a startup diagnostic written through a file-based error_log in a non-thread-safe build (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129291, an epoll use-after-free in PHP-FPM, gives root from a worker where catch_workers_output is on and the FPM master runs as root (PHP, 2026-11-19). NCSC.ch lists exploitation as unknown with no public proof of concept referenced, and watchTowr reports none as of 2026-11-20 (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19; watchTowr, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
PHP 8.5 without php.ini-production settings is exposed to CVE-2026-129474 on the defaults, when an application path enters a magic method (PHP, 2026-11-19). For CVE-2026-129289, PHP-FPM servers whose front end keeps FastCGI backend connections open (nginx fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi enablereuse=on, HAProxy in FastCGI mode) and whose applications open php://input without consuming it, which the PHP advisory says some frameworks do; standard nginx and Apache setups are outside the demonstrated attack (PHP, 2026-11-19). The session flaws need an object gadget chain in the application, and the version is shown by php -v on the host or in the container image.
Detection
In web and proxy access logs, malformed multipart/form-data bodies sent to endpoints whose application opens php://input without consuming it, followed by PHP execution that no logged request explains; in process telemetry, a shell or network tool spawned by the PHP-FPM worker, which follows from worker-level code execution.
Defender takeaway
Move the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, to the fixed build of its branch and restart PHP-FPM; where that waits, turn FastCGI connection reuse off (PHP, 2026-11-19). PHP 8.1 hosts need a newer branch for CVE-2026-129291 (PHP, 2026-11-19).

item.title: vCenter auth bypass exploited since September (GTIG), no workaround: update to 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 or 9.1.1.0200
item.description: Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0009 of 2026-11-19 fixes CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter that needs only network access to vCenter (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with no workaround and, in Broadcom's words, an emergency change. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited it from early September 2026 to move from a compromised remote-support appliance to vCenter, forge administrator SAML sessions and extract domain-controller data from guest virtual disks on ESXi; Broadcom's advisory does not state exploitation. Fixed builds are 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200, 9.1.1.0200 and VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.5, and vCenter 7.0 has no public fix.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-123890 +4exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-123890, VMware vCenter Server: an unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Directory Service gives an administrator session; GTIG reports the suspected China-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited it from early September, Broadcom lists no workaround; fixed in 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0009 of 2026-11-19 fixes CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter: an actor with network access can bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access without credentials (CVSS 3.1 9.8) (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). Broadcom lists no workaround, calls the issue an emergency change and does not state exploitation (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). Broadcom credits Mandiant with the report (Broadcom, 2026-11-19), and Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited it in early September 2026 with its BONESAW utility, according to forensic evidence (GTIG, 2026-11-19). GTIG describes one intrusion that reached an internal vCenter from a Remote Support appliance compromised through the earlier BeyondTrust zero-day and names no victim sector or country (GTIG, 2026-11-19); BleepingComputer notes that Broadcom has not confirmed the exploitation (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-19).

The flaw is a session-key disclosure over DCE/RPC in the rpc_srp_verifier service on TCP 2012 that yields an authenticated administrator@vsphere.local session; BONESAW then read the Directory Service database, extracted the SAML signing key and created an SSO administrator, SAWSNAKE forged administrator SAML assertions, and the actor switched SSH on through the appliance management API, took the master symmetric key and the PostgreSQL credential file, switched SSH off again, logged in to ESXi hosts, planted an authorized_keys entry and extracted the domain database, registry hives and DNS data from Windows guest virtual disks before copying an archive out over SCP (GTIG, 2026-11-19).

Broadcom's response matrix names the fixes: vCenter 9.1 in 9.1.1.0200, 9.0 in 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 in 8.0 U3m, VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x in 5.2.5 through KB88287 and Telco Cloud through KB463116; vCenter 7.0 has no public fix, and extended-support customers contact Broadcom Support (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). The 8.0 U3m and 9.0.2.0200 updates block later upgrades to VCF 9.1.1 until 9.1.2 (Broadcom, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
VCenter 7.0, 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 before the fixed builds; the only stated prerequisite is network access to vCenter, and GTIG's actor reached it from an internal Linux appliance, so exposure does not require an internet-facing vCenter (Broadcom, 2026-11-19; GTIG, 2026-11-19). The running build is in the vSphere Client Summary tab or in PowerCLI (Broadcom, 2026-11-19).
Detection
In the vCenter appliance management audit log, SSH switched on and then off again, a new local or SSO administrator, and reads of the Directory Service database, the master key and the PostgreSQL credential file; in network telemetry, sweeps of ports 2012, 5480 and 9080 from a Linux appliance that is not a management host; on ESXi, logins as vpxuser or root, a new authorized_keys entry and a hidden directory on a VMFS volume (GTIG, 2026-11-19). GTIG advises hardening the vCenter appliance beyond patching, and because BONESAW extracts the SAML signing key and the actor created accounts, the compromise check covers SSO and local administrators, signing material and ESXi keys from early September on (GTIG, 2026-11-19).

Triage: SSH enablement through the management API alone does not identify this activity; in GTIG's case it followed internal port sweeps from a non-management appliance and was reversed after the credential reads (GTIG, 2026-11-19).

Defender takeaway
Treat the update as an emergency change and plan around vCenter 7.0, which has no public fix; until it is in, GTIG's hardening guidance lists dropping inbound TCP 2012 from non-allowlisted addresses, to be tested first because the port carries SSO traffic (GTIG, 2026-11-19; Broadcom, 2026-11-19).

item.title: Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep
item.description: Cyderes' Howler Cell recovered a Go toolkit that wraps OpenConnect for FortiGate and NetExtender for SonicWall, a credential file of more than 500 FortiGate entries mixing default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, and VPN connection logs showing sustained root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments in May and June 2026. Once the tunnel is up the orchestrator maps internal routes and enumerates Active Directory over LDAP, while port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation are manual tools. Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking initial access broker and malware-as-a-service seller and names no victim, vulnerability or firmware version.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

tcherber: Cyderes finds an access broker's Go toolkit with VPN clients for FortiGate and SonicWall that, once a tunnel is up, maps internal routes and sweeps Active Directory over LDAP; a credential file mixes default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords (more than 500 FortiGate entries) and connection logs show root-level tunnels into multiple victims in May and June 2026

Cyderes' Howler Cell identified a database holding more than 500 FortiGate VPN credential entries and VPN connection records showing successful root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments during May and June 2026 (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). The recovered Go toolkit wraps OpenConnect with --protocol=fortinet for FortiGate, with a 30-second reconnect loop that keeps the tunnel up, and NetExtender for SonicWall, whose wrapper probes seven login URL paths and ten page patterns to find the authentication domain (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). The credential file mixes default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, which Cyderes reads as both brute-force harvesting and credential-dump sourcing; the broker's forum advert claims the access came from brute-forcing and an "exploit toolkit", which Cyderes relays without confirming (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).

The orchestrator launches the FortiGate client in the background with a 20-second stabilization delay, maps internal subnets and gateways from the established tunnel, and runs an LDAP module that enumerates users, groups, domain structure and domain controllers; port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation sit in separate tools that the operator runs by hand (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking operator working as both an initial access broker and a malware-as-a-service provider, with operations ongoing as of September 2026, and notes that the handle comes from a build-path username that one machine or several could share (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). VMRay independently links the same build path to Zer0day Stealer and ENIGMA Locker and calls the same developer the likely author of an HVNC remote-control sample, without mentioning VPN access brokerage (VMRay, 2026-09-01).

Exposure
A FortiGate or SonicWall VPN gateway reachable from the internet that accepts a local account with a default or guessed password, or a password that appears in a credential dump; Cyderes names no vulnerability or firmware version and does not discuss multi-factor authentication (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).
Detection
VPN gateway logs for successful logins by default-named accounts and for repeated reconnect attempts from one source about every 30 seconds, the interval of the FortiGate client's retry loop; after the tunnel is up, route parsing and a broad LDAP enumeration of users, groups and domain controllers from an address in the VPN pool follow from the toolkit's orchestrator (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Audit VPN credentials on FortiGate and SonicWall appliances, which is Cyderes' own recommendation, and treat default-named accounts and dumped passwords as the entry the toolkit relies on (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).

item.title: Symantec: attacker ran SYSTEM commands on a domain controller through CyberPower PowerPanel Business, then took ntds.dit
item.description: Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business, UPS-management software, as an execution channel on a Windows domain controller: scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder run through the ppbed.exe service as SYSTEM, and the operator iterated scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, then side-loaded an implant. Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console (public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access) and names no actor.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

CyberPower PowerPanel Business as a SYSTEM script channel on a domain controller: Symantec traces ntds.dit extraction with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss and a side-loaded implant to scripts that the UPS-management service ppbed.exe runs as SYSTEM; Symantec does not say how the console was reached and no actor is named

Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business (PPB), software that manages UPS devices, as the execution channel on a Windows domain controller (Symantec, 2026-11-18). Scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder and staged first under temp\profile\extcmd, are run by the PPB service ppbed.exe as SYSTEM, so the commands of the chain have ppbed.exe as their ancestor and the lineage runs ppbed.exe, cmd.exe, powershell.exe and then the implant (Symantec, 2026-11-18). The attacker pushed the scripts to the PPB web service endpoint /local/rest/v1/file/upload on TCP port 3052, worked hands-on, iterating scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, and then side-loaded the implant, an old trusted executable paired with an unknown DLL in a user-profile path (Symantec, 2026-11-18). The channel is a documented product function: CyberPower describes user-programmable command executions for event actions (CyberPower, 2026-11-19), and Symantec notes the attacker did not use power events to trigger them (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console; public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access, and it names no actor, victim sector or product version (Symantec, 2026-11-18). CISA's 2024 advisory lists PowerPanel Business 4.9.0 and prior as affected by weaknesses fixed in version 4.10.1 or later, which Symantec does not cite (CISA, 2024-05-02).

Exposure
Every host that runs PPB, a domain controller above all, whose web service on TCP 3052 a hostile network or a compromised administrator account can reach; Symantec says to audit the extcmd and temp\profile\extcmd paths of every PPB host against the product defaults (Symantec, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Process-creation lineage with ppbed.exe as the ancestor of cmd.exe or powershell.exe, every script staged under extcmd, whatever its name, certutil downloads and decodes, curl downloads and powershell -ep bypass loading .NET code in memory, inbound requests to TCP 3052 from addresses that do not administer the UPS, and on a domain controller ntdsutil, esentutl and new shadow copies; an unexpected DLL next to a trusted binary in a user-profile path marks the side-loaded implant (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

Triage: the activity looks like a power-management product launching cmd.exe, which defenders may dismiss as a routine power-related recovery process; scripts or event-to-command assignments that no administrator configured, children that are not shutdown or notification routines (which follows from the mechanism) and the absence of a preceding power event separate it from benign use (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

Defender takeaway
Treat PPB hosts as privileged execution surfaces: restrict TCP port 3052 to named administrator hosts, change the default administrator password and keep PPB patched, since CISA names 4.10.1 as the fixed build for its 2024 advisory (Symantec, 2026-11-18; CISA, 2024-05-02); where the techniques Symantec lists are found, assume Active Directory credentials are exposed and plan a krbtgt reset and wider credential rotation (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

item.title: Airlock Gateway: Smart Form Protection buffer overflow can crash or take over the gateway; update to 8.5.3 or 8.6.1
item.description: Airlock (Ergon) published CVE-2026-19707 on 2026-11-18: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response can overflow a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature of Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0, possibly causing denial of service or remote code execution against the gateway, when the feature is enabled on a mapping whose backend returns certain multi-byte HTML character references (CVSS 4.0 9.5, high attack complexity). The fix is in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no source reports exploitation, and Airlock says a compromised gateway could also affect the protection of the other backends behind it.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-19707NATOA2

CVE-2026-19707, Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response overflows a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature and can cause denial of service or code execution on the gateway; fixed in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.5)

Airlock (Ergon) published CVE-2026-19707 on 2026-11-18 as the CNA. It says attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response can exploit the Smart Form Protection feature of Airlock Gateway 8.5.2 and earlier and 8.6.0, possibly leading to a denial of service or remote code execution against the gateway, and that the issue is fixed in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18). The attack needs Smart Form Protection, or the corresponding expert settings, enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references, and the overflow happens while the gateway parses that response; the response can come from a malicious or compromised backend or from a trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, for example an application that stores and serves user-provided HTML files (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18). The record scores CVSS 4.0 9.5 with high attack complexity and says that compromising the gateway could also affect the availability and protection of other backends deployed behind it (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18). Airlock's release notes for 8.6.1 and 8.5.3 list a fix for a buffer overflow when decoding HTML entities in the same releases, without a CVE id (Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19; Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19). Airlock's support table shows 8.5 supported until 06/2027, 8.4 past its end of support in 08/2026 and 8.3 no longer supported (Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 or 8.6.0 with Smart Form Protection enabled, which Airlock's documentation says requires URL encryption to be activated first, on a mapping whose backend can return attacker-supplied HTML (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18; Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19). Gateways on 8.4 and older are outside support and have no listed fix.
Detection
The record names no indicator; gateway process crashes or restarts and unexpected child processes on the gateway, and backend responses with unusual multi-byte HTML character references, follow from the mechanism (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18).
Defender takeaway
Update to 8.5.3 or 8.6.1, backends that serve user-supplied HTML behind a gateway with Smart Form Protection first; no source reports exploitation, so the order follows exposure rather than a known campaign (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18).

item.title: Idunno.AntiCsrf (ASP.NET WebForms) unauthenticated deserialization RCE exploited, no patch: remove the module
item.description: Mandiant published CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, an open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms last released in December 2008: any anonymously reachable page that does not opt out passes a crafted CSRF form field to an unvalidated deserializer, so one POST runs code in the IIS worker process (CVSS 4.0 9.3). Mandiant states that exploitation in the wild has been observed, names no actor, and says the project has no active maintainer or official patch, so the fix is to remove the module, and Mandiant adds that environments with evidence of exploitation should rotate the secrets held in the web configuration and inspect the web root.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-131914exploitedNATOB2

CVE-2026-131914, Idunno.AntiCsrf 0.9.1 and earlier, a defunct anti-CSRF module for ASP.NET WebForms: one unauthenticated POST with a crafted CSRF form field is deserialized without validation and runs code in the IIS worker process; Mandiant observed exploitation in the wild and no patch exists, so the module has to be removed (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

Mandiant published advisory MNDT-2026-0048 and CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, a defunct open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms, last released as 0.9.1 Beta in December 2008 on the since-retired CodePlex platform and with no active maintainer or official patch (Mandiant, 2026-11-18). In the module's PreRequestHandlerExecute step, once the CSRF cookie and the CSRF form field are both non-empty, it deserializes the form field with a parameterless ObjectStateFormatter, which performs no MAC, signature, encryption or machineKey validation and enforces no SerializationBinder restrictions, so a crafted serialized .NET object in that field runs code in the IIS worker process, w3wp.exe; one POST with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token suffices (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

The module runs before the page lifecycle, so any anonymously reachable .aspx page, or any page that relies on application-level session checks inside Page_Load, is reachable unless it opts out through ISuppressCsrfCheck or the SuppressCsrfCheck attribute; pipeline-level authentication rules run earlier and keep anonymous requests away from pages they protect (Mandiant, 2026-11-18). After the sink the module raises its own error, so the response is HTTP 302 when customErrors is active and HTTP 500 when its mode is Off, and recompiled or customised copies keep the sink under different file hashes (Mandiant, 2026-11-18). Mandiant states that active exploitation in the wild has been observed, names no actor, and says Google's FLARE team completed the root-cause analysis during an incident-response investigation on 2026-11-04 (Mandiant, 2026-11-18); the ENISA record scores the flaw CVSS 4.0 9.3 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
An ASP.NET WebForms application whose Web.config registers Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule under httpModules or modules, or whose bin directory holds Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll; Mandiant says to search by name, not by hash (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).
Detection
IIS logs for anomalous POST requests to .aspx endpoints that return 302 or 500 with elevated request size (cs-bytes, where logged), carrying the module's default cookie __CSRFCOOKIE and form field __CSRFTOKEN, and process-creation telemetry for children of w3wp.exe, which follows from code execution in the worker; if the csrfSettings section is omitted from Web.config, a setter bug overwrites the fallback form field name with RaiseException, so the default field name is not a reliable hunting key on every deployment (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

Triage: the module's own tokens are a GUID cookie and a short serialized GUID in the form field, so a cookie that is not a GUID, or a large Base64 value in the CSRF form field, is not legitimate token traffic (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

Defender takeaway
Remove the module and its DLL and replace it with a supported anti-forgery mechanism, since no patch exists; on environments with evidence of exploitation, Mandiant says to rotate all secrets stored in Web.config and applicationHost.config, machineKey and encryption keys and database credentials included, and to inspect the web roots for unauthorized files (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

item.title: REDCap unauthenticated survey-to-RCE chain exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 16.0.49, 17.3.10 or 17.4.4
item.description: Securifera described CVE-2026-90817 on 2026-09-27, a five-step chain in Vanderbilt's REDCap research-data platform that turns a request to a public survey into code execution on the server without authentication, given a valid public survey hash (CVSS 3.1 9.8). Unit 42 reported it exploited on 2026-10-07 to install Monero miners behind a transient web shell, with cron, SSH-key and shell-profile persistence, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18. The fixed builds are 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-90817exploitedNATOB1

CVE-2026-90817, REDCap 13.3.0 up to 16.0.48 LTS, 17.3.9 LTS and 17.4.3 Standard: an unauthenticated chain from a public survey request through the Data Import controller to code execution on the server, exploited as of 2026-10-07 for cryptocurrency mining and listed by CISA; fixed in 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Securifera, which found the flaw, describes a chain of five faults in REDCap, the research-data platform from Vanderbilt University. The public survey handler checks the passthrough value in two forms, so a double-encoded value reaches the root index.php dispatcher while the route restriction is skipped; the project user-rights object is built before the respondent identity exists, so the public context receives the Data Import privilege and the POST CSRF check is skipped because NOAUTH is defined; the Data Import commit path trusts the posted file name as a local path or PHP stream; the byte-order-mark cleanup writes changed bytes back to the same stream, which turns a CSV cleanup into an arbitrary overwrite; and a compiled-template cache file is then rendered as PHP through a route that works without a login (Securifera, 2026-09-27). An attacker needs only a valid survey hash, with no account, project membership, session cookie, role or CSRF token (Securifera, 2026-09-27); Securifera's repository publishes a proof of concept (Securifera repository, 2026-10-01).

Unit 42's note of 2026-10-07 reports active exploitation: an unauthenticated POST to a public survey URL stages a transient Blade-template web shell under the temp cache, run by php-fpm with the web server's permissions, which executes a Base64 bash cradle entirely in memory and pipes a payload disguised as a JPEG into bash (Unit 42, 2026-10-07). The chain deploys Monero miners, run with randomized syslog-themed process names, with at least four live workers; persistence is a modified crontab, an RSA public key appended to the authorized_keys of every accessible profile and an edited ~/.profile, and the attackers unset HISTFILE and purge the bash history (Unit 42, 2026-10-07). CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-18).

Google's GTIG reported in June 2026 that the PRC-nexus cluster UNC6508 had exploited internet-facing REDCap servers of North American academic and medical organisations (Google GTIG, 2026-06-15). REDCap 13.3.0 through 16.0.48 LTS, 17.3.9 LTS and 17.4.3 Standard are vulnerable (Pentest-Tools, 2026-10-23); the CVE record names 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard as the upgrade targets (OpenCVE, 2026-09-20).

Exposure
Any REDCap server from 13.3.0 to the builds above that serves a public survey; the attack needs a valid survey hash (Securifera, 2026-09-27).
Detection
Web access logs for POSTs to public survey URLs with a double percent-encoded passthrough and a Data Import route (Unit 42, 2026-10-07) and, where a WAF or proxy logs request bodies, a php:// stream in the file-name field (Securifera, 2026-09-27); transient Blade-template files under the web temp cache, a web-server worker or php-fpm spawning bash, and miner processes started under syslog-style names (Unit 42, 2026-10-07). Securifera's proof of concept deletes its injected cache so that REDCap regenerates a clean copy, so a clean cache does not prove the server was not hit (Securifera, 2026-09-27).

Triage: the survey flow is supposed to allow only the PDF route (PdfController:index), so a public survey request that reaches the Data Import controller or carries a stream wrapper in the file-name field is not benign (Securifera, 2026-09-27).

Defender takeaway
Upgrade now and check crontabs, authorized_keys, ~/.profile and processes on any server that was reachable on an older build, because an upgrade removes none of the persistence Unit 42 lists (Unit 42, 2026-10-07).
