item.title: NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update 1.31.9, 1.30.7 or Plus 37.3.0.1
item.description: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, while NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Cisco and Siemens list products with fixes pending or none, and Fortinet is still investigating its portfolio.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-123007 +4updatedNATOA1

NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated memory-corruption flaws (CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 in HTTP/2, CVE-2026-121810 in HTTP/3, CVE-2026-123634 in the resolver, CVE-2026-113425 in the mail proxy) can lead to code execution as the worker process; fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, Rapid7 proof of concept public, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

F5 and the nginx project published the nginx2root fixes (nginx.org, 2026-11-18); CERT-EU counts five vulnerabilities, all able to lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the NGINX worker process (CERT-EU, 2026-11-18). CVE-2026-123007 is an HTTP/2 flow-control overflow: cancelling queued response data makes nginx use an invalid length when copying a later response (Rapid7, 2026-11-18), and Wiz demonstrated code execution on nginx serving ordinary static files (Wiz Research, 2026-11-18).

Rapid7 published a working proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007 against nginx 1.31.8; the exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic and likely fails with concurrent clients (Rapid7, 2026-11-18; Rapid7 repository, 2026-11-18). Rapid7 says execution has the worker's permissions and root is not established; F5, as CERT.at relays it, frames the base effect as worker crashes, with code execution possible where ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed, which Wiz says attackers can do by reading memory first (translated from German) (Rapid7, 2026-11-18; CERT.at, 2026-11-18; Wiz Research, 2026-11-18). CERT-EU reports no exploitation in the wild, NCSC.ch rates exploitation unknown with a proof of concept available, and NCSC-NL expects large-scale exploitation once proof-of-concept code is public (translated from Dutch) (CERT-EU, 2026-11-18; NCSC.ch, 2026-11-18; NCSC-NL, 2026-11-18).

The fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 (nginx.org, 2026-11-18). CERT.at lists NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1 as fixing four of the five (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-113425); it also says 37.2.0.1 and 37.0.7.1 already carry the fix for CVE-2026-123633 but stay affected by CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-121810, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update (translated from German) (CERT.at, 2026-11-18).

Exposure
An nginx build from the first affected release of each flaw (1.9.5, 1.19.7, 0.6.18, 1.25.0 and 0.5.33) up to 1.31.8 whose configuration uses the feature: an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 listener, the resolver with variable proxy_pass destinations plus mirror or SSI, or the mail proxy with auth_http (nginx.org, 2026-11-18; Xint, 2026-11-18). A distribution backport can fix a flaw without changing the version nginx -v reports (Xint, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Process-creation or audit telemetry for any program started by the worker's user, since a normal nginx worker runs no external programs and that is the clearest sign of success; worker exits and core dumps in the error log mark attempts, not successes (Xint, 2026-11-18; CERT-EU, 2026-11-18). Network flow data showing a long-lived TLS connection with fast-growing received volume and little sent data, and many short connections from the same address, hints at CVE-2026-123007 (Xint, 2026-11-18).

Triage: a large upload is a legitimate cause of an inbound-heavy connection and workers crash for unrelated reasons, so a program started by the worker is the discriminator, not the traffic shape alone (Xint, 2026-11-18).

Defender takeaway
Update and restart nginx, because a configuration reload does not replace the running executable; disabling HTTP/2 on exposed listeners blocks only the two HTTP/2 flaws, and Xint gives interim measures for the others: a fixed upstream group in place of request-time DNS lookups for CVE-2026-123634, no QUIC listeners for CVE-2026-121810 and bound or firewalled mail listeners for CVE-2026-113425 (Xint, 2026-11-18). An empty execution-audit result after the update cannot rule out an earlier compromise, and Xint chained CVE-2026-123007 with a separate Linux kernel SCTP flaw, unpatched when it published, to reach root on the host and escape a Docker container; hosts that do not use SCTP can block the module from loading (Xint, 2026-11-18).
Update21 Nov 2026 04:37 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiessourcesevidenceactionsbody

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama (virtual and M-Series) as affected by CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 only where the HTTP/2 option is enabled, and says it knows of no malicious exploitation; disabling HTTP/2 is its workaround (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-11-20). The fixed builds are PAN-OS 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6 and 11.2.16-h3; 12.1.7-h15, 11.2.10-h19 and 11.2.13-h6 carry an ETA of 2026-11-23, and 12.1.2 to 12.1.4 and 11.2.0 to 11.2.7 need no action (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-11-20).

Cisco's interim advisory (version 1.0, 2026-11-20) lists NX-OS Software, Smart PHY (fix 27.1.0, March 2027), the Intersight Virtual Appliance (1.1.9-0, December 2026), Cloud Hosted Services Vulnerability Management (1.30.7, November 2026) and Identity Services Engine 3.5 (3.5 Patch 5, December 2026) as affected, lists Catalyst Center, the SD-WAN Controller and Manager, ASA, FMC, FTD and UCS Central as not affected, and has IOS XE, IOS XR and UCS Director under investigation; its PSIRT knows of proof-of-concept code and of no malicious use (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Siemens (SSA-935812, 2026-11-20) lists Industrial Edge products as affected in all versions with no fix available and names disabling HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 on the affected listeners as the mitigation (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-20). item.title: Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI carried a Python-startup credential stealer in 1.26.1 and 1.26.2; pin 1.26.0
item.description: Socket and SafeDep report that versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's official agent-framework metapackage were published to PyPI on 2026-11-17, about 33 minutes apart, with a .pth file that runs a credential stealer whenever Python starts, so a pip install in a CI job is enough. It collects environment secrets and credential files and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Both versions were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release; how the attacker obtained publishing access is not known.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB1

Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 published on 2026-11-17, carried a credential stealer that a .pth startup hook runs every time Python starts, collecting environment secrets and requesting Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions OIDC tokens; both versions were removed and 1.26.0 is the last clean release

Socket reports that the Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package was compromised on 2026-11-17, in versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, both of which install Python startup hooks that collect credentials, environment data and cloud identity tokens and send them to a web endpoint (Socket, 2026-11-17). SafeDep, which flagged both releases independently, says the project is Microsoft's official metapackage, published under the microsoft account on PyPI, that 1.26.1 appeared at 20:35 UTC and 1.26.2 at 21:08 UTC, that each is a single wheel where earlier releases shipped a wheel and a source archive, and that both were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release (SafeDep, 2026-11-18). The attacker published 1.26.2 after 1.26.1 was gone, so removing one version did not stop it, and how it obtained publishing access is not known (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).

Nothing has to import the package: a .pth file runs on Python startup, imports a module and launches collection in a background process or thread, so a pip install in a CI job is enough (Socket, 2026-11-17; SafeDep, 2026-11-18). 1.26.1 routes through the package's own initializer, while 1.26.2 moves the payload to a new top-level module and restores the legitimate initializer byte for byte, so checking only the initializer misses it (Socket, 2026-11-17). The code matches environment variables by substring, such as TOKEN, SECRET, KEY and AZURE, reads other processes' environments and credential files for pip, npm, netrc, git, Docker, Hugging Face and Foundry, and actively requests fresh Azure managed-identity and Azure DevOps tokens, with GitHub Actions OIDC tokens added in 1.26.2; it compresses the result and posts it to a web endpoint and downloads no further code (Socket, 2026-11-17). There is no persistent on-disk marker, so fresh process trees can trigger collection again (Socket, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Any developer machine, CI job or container that installed agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 and then ran Python; lockfiles and requirements files show the installed version, and the last clean release is 1.26.0 (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Lockfiles and requirements files naming the two versions, and a .pth file added to site-packages by the package, looked for on disk without starting the environment's Python, because starting it runs the stealer again (SafeDep, 2026-11-18); outbound POSTs to a web-hook service from build and developer hosts; because the stealer requests identity tokens, review sign-in and activity logs for the managed identities and federated credentials the environment could use, from the install time onward (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).
Defender takeaway
Remove both versions, rotate every secret and federated identity a host or job could read, and pin agent-framework to a known clean version; Socket advises rotating potentially exposed credentials where either version was installed (Socket, 2026-11-17).

item.title: Mitel MiCollab: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 command injection in the conferencing component; patch KB000129195
item.description: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0012 of 2026-11-16 covers five flaws in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier, led by an unauthenticated blind command injection scored CVSS 3.1 10.0 and an unauthenticated XML injection scored 9.0 that could run commands. Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0012, first issued on 2026-11-16, covers five flaws in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier; Mitel tracks them by internal ids and its page still says the CVE identifiers it requested are not yet assigned (Mitel, 2026-11-16), while MITRE published CVE records for all five on 2026-11-19 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-19). MTLVULN-1864 lets an unauthenticated attacker conduct a blind command injection through insufficient parameter sanitization and is scored CVSS 3.1 10.0 with changed scope; MTLVULN-1862 lets an unauthenticated attacker leverage pre-staged malicious content for an XML injection that could run arbitrary commands, scored 9.0 with high attack complexity (Mitel, 2026-11-16). Three further flaws are rated Medium: an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload through weak file-type validation (MTLVULN-1861, 5.3), unauthorized access that needs a system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content (MTLVULN-1863, 5.9) and an authentication bypass (MTLVULN-1877, 5.3) (Mitel, 2026-11-16). Mitel's July advisory named 10.3 (10.3.0.18) as the release that fixed its earlier AWV command injection, so a system moved there in July is inside the new affected range (Mitel, 2026-07-22). CERT-FR lists the advisory on 2026-11-17 and BSI rates it high, describing a remote anonymous attacker who can manipulate files, run code with the service's rights and bypass security measures (CERT-FR, 2026-11-17; BSI, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier whose AWV component external users can reach; Mitel assesses only supported versions and states no branch before 10.3 (Mitel, 2026-11-16).
Detection
Child processes of the AWV service, new files in the component's upload paths and unauthenticated requests to conferencing endpoints that carry shell metacharacters or XML payloads, which follow from the command-injection, upload and XML-injection mechanisms the advisory names (Mitel, 2026-11-16).
Defender takeaway
Apply the patch now; where that waits, restrict external access to the AWV component, the mitigation Mitel names (Mitel, 2026-11-16).

item.title: Oracle CSPU: 56 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0+, six at 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic, BI; none exploited
item.description: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update of 2026-11-17 carries 655 patches, and its risk matrices mark 56 of the 62 rows scoring CVSS 3.1 9.0 or above as remotely exploitable without authentication. Six are CVSS 10.0 with changed scope, in Oracle Access Manager (three rows), WebLogic Server TopLink Integration, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition, and WebLogic Server and E-Business Suite carry further unauthenticated rows at 9.8. No source reports exploitation of any of these rows, and for attacks that need no privileges Oracle's interim measure is blocking the network protocols an attack needs.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-114835 +17NATOA2

Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update: 56 of its 62 rows at CVSS 9.0 or above are reachable over the network without authentication, six of them at CVSS 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic Server, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition; no row is marked exploited

Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update of 2026-11-17 carries 655 new patches (Oracle, 2026-11-17). Its risk matrices score 62 rows at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or above, 56 of them marked remotely exploitable without authentication and without privileges (Oracle, 2026-11-17); Tenable counts 62 critical patches across 57 CVEs (Tenable, 2026-11-17). Six of them score 10.0 with changed scope: Oracle Access Manager 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.2.1.0 in the Admin Console (CVE-2026-114835) and twice in the Authentication Engine (CVE-2026-91500, CVE-2026-91510), WebLogic Server TopLink Integration (CVE-2026-91569), Platform Security for Java (CVE-2026-114824) and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition Platform Security (CVE-2026-114784), all over HTTP (Oracle, 2026-11-17).

WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4.0 to 15.1.1.0.0 carries further unauthenticated rows at 9.8: Core over T3 and IIOP (CVE-2026-91470) and over SOAP (CVE-2026-91456), and TopLink Integration over HTTP (CVE-2026-91570, CVE-2026-91583) and TCP (CVE-2026-91585); Oracle words the T3 and IIOP row as an easily exploitable flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access compromise WebLogic Server (Oracle, 2026-11-17). E-Business Suite 12.2.3 to 12.2.15 has four unauthenticated HTTP rows at 9.8 in Attachments (CVE-2026-114880), Application Object Library (CVE-2026-114924), Applications Framework REST Services (CVE-2026-114925) and Universal Work Queue (CVE-2026-114863), and APEX and REST Data Services have two at 9.8 over HTTPS (CVE-2026-114849, CVE-2026-114850) (Oracle, 2026-11-17). Oracle's footnote says the patch for the E-Business Suite row CVE-2026-114918 also addresses CVE-2025-61882 (Oracle, 2026-11-17), which CISA lists as exploited with known ransomware use (CISA, 2026-11-17). The release also carries three rows for the Brotli flaw CVE-2026-111497 in Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools (Oracle, 2026-11-17).

Oracle's matrices carry no exploitation flag, and its interim relief is blocking the network protocols an attack requires or, for attacks that need certain privileges or package access, removing those; patches exist only for versions under Premier or Extended Support, and Oracle says earlier versions are likely affected too (Oracle, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Access Manager, WebLogic Server, E-Business Suite, APEX or REST Data Services, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition instances on the listed versions that untrusted networks can reach over HTTP, HTTPS, SOAP, TCP, T3 or IIOP (Oracle, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Apply the November 2026 patches to internet-reachable identity, middleware, ERP and APEX instances first, and until then block the protocols a row needs, T3 and IIOP for the WebLogic Core row (Oracle, 2026-11-17). Oracle names no per-flaw workaround, so unsupported versions have no vendor fix.

item.title: TYPO3: backend user to installer to admin and RCE (SA-027 Critical); Form Framework flaw SA-029 exploited; update now
item.description: TYPO3 published ten core advisories on 2026-11-17 for 10.0.0 to 14.3.11, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS. The one rated Critical (SA-027) lets a file named FIRST_INSTALL placed in the web root re-enable the installer without authentication, which creates an administrator and leads to remote code execution, and SA-026 lets any low-privileged backend user create such a file. TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework that can become cross-site scripting through uploaded HTML, is known to be actively exploited, naming no actor or victim.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-119623 +9exploitedNATOA2

TYPO3 core security releases of 2026-11-17 (ten advisories): a low-privileged backend user can write a file into the web root and re-enable the unauthenticated installer, which creates an administrator and leads to code execution (SA-026, SA-027 Critical), and TYPO3 states that a Form Framework flaw (SA-029) is actively exploited; fixed in 14.3.12, 13.4.40, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS

TYPO3 released ten core advisories on 2026-11-17, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS (TYPO3, 2026-11-17); versions 10.0.0 to 10.4.62, 11.0.0 to 11.5.56, 12.0.0 to 12.4.51, 13.0.0 to 13.4.39 and 14.0.0 to 14.3.11 are affected (TYPO3 SA-027, 2026-11-17). SA-027 is rated Critical: placing a file whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the public web root or the project root re-enables the installer on a configured instance without authentication, which allows changing the database connection and creating a new administrator and system maintainer account, and that leads to remote code execution; leftover or restored marker files also work (TYPO3 SA-027, 2026-11-17). SA-026, rated High, supplies the file: the backend endpoint for adding online media accepts a target folder in the fallback storage, which points to the public web root, so any authenticated low-privileged backend user can create media files with a partially controllable name there (TYPO3 SA-026, 2026-11-17).

TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework, is known to be actively exploited, and names no actor, victim or behaviour (TYPO3 SA-029, 2026-11-17). A failed upload shows the raw storage error with the upload sub-folder, so an attacker can derive the public URL of an uploaded file, and where the form accepts HTML this becomes cross-site scripting unless the web server applies TYPO3's recommended Content-Security-Policy to the upload folder (TYPO3 SA-029, 2026-11-17). SA-032 closes the matching gap, an empty allowedMimeTypes list that was treated as no restriction and let unauthenticated visitors upload HTML or SVG to a public folder (TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17). SA-028 lets ImageMagick's MVG coder disclose any web-server-readable file through a processed image; it needs ImageMagick with its default configuration allowing the MVG coder, and unauthenticated visitors reach it where such an upload form exists (TYPO3 SA-028, 2026-11-17). SA-025 is an Import/Export path traversal that writes arbitrary files and needs an administrator or a user enabled for import (TYPO3 SA-025, 2026-11-17). Four lesser flaws are an incomplete open-redirect fix (SA-030), page-cache flooding where cHash validation is not enforced (SA-031), file-dump token reuse (SA-033) and an SSRF in the 14.x Dashboard RSS widget (SA-034) (TYPO3 SA-030, 2026-11-17; SA-031; SA-033; SA-034).

Exposure
Any TYPO3 instance on an affected version; the installer chain needs only a low-privileged backend account, and the Form Framework flaws need a public form with an upload element (TYPO3 SA-026, 2026-11-17; TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17).
Detection
Files whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the web root or project root, and administrator or system maintainer accounts nobody created (TYPO3 SA-027, 2026-11-17); HTML or SVG files in the form upload folder and web-server logs for direct requests to them (TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Update to the fixed release of each branch now. After updating, configure at least one allowed MIME type for every upload element, because an empty list now refuses uploads (TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17); on 14.x configure the dashboard_rss allowed hosts, because the update alone does not mitigate SA-034 (TYPO3 SA-034, 2026-11-17); and deliver the form upload folder with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, which nginx needs configured by hand (TYPO3 SA-029, 2026-11-17); and, after updating, configure image formats outside the default raster set, such as psd or ppm, explicitly in fileExtensionToMimeType so ImageMagick still processes them (TYPO3 SA-028, 2026-11-17).

item.description: Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-017 (CVE-2026-132165, Critical 18 of 25) and SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166, Moderately critical, not directly exploitable) on 2026-11-18: under specific conditions an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, which can lead to site takeover or remote code execution. Fixed in 11.4.13, 11.3.22 and 10.6.22, the only workaround is securing the installer, and no source reports exploitation, although the Security Team had warned that exploits might be developed within hours or days.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-132165 +1updatedNATOA2

Drupal core 11.4.13, 11.3.22 and 10.6.22 fix CVE-2026-132165 (SA-CORE-2026-017, Critical): under specific conditions an attacker can use the installer to reinstall Drupal, which can lead to site takeover or remote code execution; the only workaround is securing the installer, and no exploitation is reported

Drupal shipped its announced core security release on 2026-11-18. SA-CORE-2026-017 (CVE-2026-132165, rated Critical 18 of 25, with access complexity Complex, access none, exploit status Proof, meaning a proof of concept exists with documented methods for developing an exploit in the wild, and target distribution Uncommon, meaning only uncommon module configurations are exploitable) says that under specific conditions an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, which can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166, Moderately critical 14 of 25) is a gadget chain that Drupal says is not directly exploitable: a separate vulnerability must be present to let an attacker pass unsafe input to unserialize() (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18).

Both advisories cover core before 10.6.22, from 11.0.0 before 11.3.22 and from 11.4.0 before 11.4.13, fixed in 11.4.13, 11.3.22 and 10.6.22; Drupal 11.2.x and below and 10.5.x and below are end-of-life and receive no security coverage (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). The only workaround Drupal gives is to secure the installer; it adds that some exploit paths are mitigated if the web server cannot write to or change permissions on settings.php, and that sites on Drupal Steward are already protected from SA-CORE-2026-017's known attack vectors (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). The pre-announcement had warned that exploits might be developed within hours or days (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-16); NCSC.ch's Security Hub rated exploitation unknown on 2026-11-17 (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-17), and neither advisory reports exploitation.

Exposure
Any Drupal site on core before 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13, though Drupal's own rating says only uncommon module configurations are exploitable, and every site on an end-of-life line, which has no fix; NCSC-NL says the condition arises when the installer is not correctly secured or removed after the initial installation (translated from Dutch) (NCSC-NL, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Web access logs for requests to the installer on a site that is already installed, which follows from the mechanism; Drupal's advisory names no indicators of compromise.
Defender takeaway
Update each site to 11.4.13, 11.3.22 or 10.6.22 now and move end-of-life sites to a supported branch; where the update waits, secure the installer. Drupal advises upgrading even behind Steward, in case additional attack vectors are discovered (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18).

item.title: RIKEN Fugaku: intruder entered via the public status dashboard, took users' SSH keys and tried them elsewhere
item.description: RIKEN says that between 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13 an external party used the publicly accessible web page showing Fugaku's operating status to enter its internal operational network, tampered with internal servers (some with malicious programs) and took or may have taken home-directory files, user-authentication data and credentials users had stored for other systems, such as SSH private keys and access keys. Up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 Rikyu users are affected, RIKEN confirmed that some of the stolen credentials were tried against other systems, and it suspended Fugaku on 2026-11-14. How the dashboard was breached is still under investigation, and RIKEN names no actor.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

RIKEN Fugaku and Rikyu supercomputers: an intruder entered the internal operational network through the internet-facing operating-status dashboard, planted malicious programs on internal servers and took users' stored SSH private keys and access keys, then tried them on other systems

RIKEN's Center for Computational Science says that between 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13 an external third party entered Fugaku's internal operational network through the publicly accessible web page that displays the supercomputer's operating status, and that the exact method is still under investigation (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). The intruder tampered with multiple internal servers, some of them with malicious programs, and took or may have taken files in users' home directories and user-authentication data, including credentials users had stored for connecting to other systems, such as SSH private keys and access keys; up to 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 Rikyu users are affected (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). RIKEN has confirmed that the intruder tried some of the obtained credentials against other systems and is checking whether damage or secondary misuse followed (RIKEN, 2026-11-17).

RIKEN and the external provider that maintains the system began investigating suspicious network traffic on 2026-11-12, confirmed the access on 2026-11-13 and suspended Fugaku on 2026-11-14 (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). It replaced the administrative keys, invalidated the public keys all users use to log in and halted all running and queued jobs, and it names no actor; it says there is no evidence yet that research data was exfiltrated (RIKEN, 2026-11-17; BleepingComputer, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
A shared compute or research system whose operating-status page is reachable from the internet and sits on a network path to its internal operations servers, and whose users keep SSH private keys or cloud access keys in their home directories (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). Relevant to Swiss research and high-performance-computing operators as a transferable pattern of exposure.
Detection
Authentications to other systems with keys that belong to users of the affected host, arriving from unfamiliar addresses, and changes or unknown programs on the servers that run the system's operation; RIKEN's own reviews cover the network configuration and the rebuilding of compromised servers (RIKEN, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Treat every private key and access key stored on a compromised host as stolen: RIKEN asks users to revoke the matching public key at each external service where it is authorised and to generate a new pair, and to replace any other stored credential through the service concerned (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). A status page that is public should not give a route into the operations network.

item.title: Barracuda: an unretired vendor cloud key led an ARTEX-consistent intruder across ten accounts in 44 hours
item.description: Barracuda says an attacker used a valid cloud access key that it had issued to an AI-sector vendor for a past project and never retired, between 2026-11-01 04:33 and 2026-11-02 23:31 UTC, reading stored secrets and moving through about ten cloud accounts, a data analytics system, a source-code token and Kubernetes clusters. One system reached stores the credentials Barracuda Managed XDR uses to collect data from customers' connected systems; Barracuda found no direct evidence they were accessed, treated them as exposed and asked the customers it notified to revoke and recreate them. Barracuda says the activity is consistent with ARTEX, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework, and that this shows how the attacker worked, not who it was.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

Barracuda's own account of a 44-hour intrusion into its cloud: a key given to an AI vendor and never retired, found in that vendor's compromised development environment, led an intruder across about ten cloud accounts to Kubernetes; notified Managed XDR customers must recreate their integration credentials

Barracuda says the attacker did not break in but used a valid cloud access key that Barracuda had issued to a third-party vendor, a company working in AI, for an earlier project and had not retired when the work ended (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). The key had been stored in a configuration file in the vendor's GitHub repository, which was exposed when the vendor's development environment was compromised (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). The first call with the key came on 2026-11-01 at 04:33 UTC; within minutes the attacker was mapping what the key reached and reading stored secrets such as AWS access keys and Azure service principal secrets, and each secret opened the next system, from cloud accounts to a data analytics system, to a source-code access token and on to Kubernetes clusters (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). In just under four hours on 2026-11-02 it pushed short-lived branches to a handful of repositories to trigger a build workflow written to print the build system's secrets into the job log, encoded so that log masking would not hide them, and its last recorded activity was at 23:31 UTC, about 10 cloud accounts and 44 hours after the start (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11).

In a Kubernetes cluster the attacker deployed a container that mounted the underlying server's file system read-only, enough to harvest that server's credentials, and tried to create a new administrative cloud identity, which was blocked (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). On servers where it had a shell, its commands searched for environment variables named WALLET, MNEMONIC, SEED and PRIV, Ethereum keystore files, extended private keys, seed phrase files and Kubernetes secrets with wallet-related names, and Barracuda calls the activity consistent with a financially motivated actor seeking cryptocurrency and reusable credentials (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). Barracuda says the resource names, the sequence of activity and the credential and wallet hunting routines match ARTEX, which many groups use, so the match shows how the attacker operated, not who it was (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11).

Exposure
A system the attacker reached stores the credentials Barracuda Managed XDR uses to collect data from customers' connected systems such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and endpoint security platforms; only organisations using the API integration for Managed XDR Cloud or Monitored Endpoint are affected, and Barracuda notified those with potentially affected credentials (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). Logging in that environment was not detailed enough to rule out access to the credentials (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). Relevant as a supplier incident for any organisation whose monitoring runs on Managed XDR, and as a worked example of ARTEX-style cloud tradecraft.
Detection
In cloud control-plane audit logs, a long-lived key used by a non-vendor address, secret-store reads followed by use of those secrets in other accounts, resources named with the letter i followed by digits and no hyphen, short-lived branches in a handful of repositories that trigger a workflow, and container deployments that mount the node's file system (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13; Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11).
Defender takeaway
A notified customer revokes and recreates its integration credentials and reviews connected-system activity since 2026-11-01 (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). Barracuda's own lesson is to remove standing credentials, especially long-lived keys held by third parties (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11), and to expire vendor credentials when an engagement ends (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13).

item.title: Mandiant: COLD RELIC turns one cloud compromise into the pretext for the next; enrolled passkeys outlive password resets
item.description: Mandiant reports that COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (Star Blizzard), reused the staff directory and identities stolen from one US organisation in late 2025 to impersonate a contact when approaching a second in 2026. In the late-2025 case it took over a Super Admin account through push-notification fatigue, kept access with enrolled passkeys, MFA backup codes and rogue MFA devices that survived password and session resets, and exported the whole tenant; in 2026 it phished Entra ID credentials and registered a new MFA device to download one user's drive. GTIG names government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America as targets and says new phishing operations continued into November 2026.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

COLD RELIC: Mandiant shows the FSB-linked group reusing data stolen from one US organisation as the impersonation pretext for the next, then holding cloud tenants through MFA push fatigue and enrolled passkeys, backup codes and MFA devices that survive password and session resets

Mandiant reports a series of linked intrusions in which COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (also Star Blizzard, Callisto and Gossamer Bear), turned data stolen in one US organisation into the pretext for the next (GTIG, 2026-11-17). GTIG cites a US Department of Justice assessment that the group operates within Russia's FSB and names government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America among its targets (GTIG, 2026-11-17). In 2026 the operators approached a second US organisation over an encrypted messaging app while impersonating an employee of the first, shared phishing links that stole Entra ID credentials and tokens and sent the victim on to document lures matching the conversation, and registered a new MFA device on the account (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

In the late-2025 case the operators used the stolen credentials of a Super Admin account from a US residential proxy network close to the victim, pressed the user with MFA push notifications until one was accepted, registered a device model new to the tenant and kept access with passkeys, MFA backup codes and rogue MFA devices (GTIG, 2026-11-17). They took the whole cloud drive by mass sharing to an operator-run mailbox and by direct download, queried the admin investigation and email audit logs to check defensive visibility, viewed, modified and deleted Alert Center notifications, exported the employee list and ran a tenant-wide Customer Takeout export (GTIG, 2026-11-17). Access lasted several months through OAuth mail sync to an external client and re-authentication with enrolled passkeys that survived password and session resets, and in one case a password reset without revoking sessions did not evict the operators (GTIG, 2026-11-17). They searched for credentials, personnel data and .pst archives (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Google Workspace tenants, and Entra ID tenants that federate sign-in to Workspace as in the second case, whose privileged or staff accounts accept push, SMS or voice MFA or let users enrol passkeys, backup codes and devices without a second approval (GTIG, 2026-11-17).
Detection
In authentication logs, repeated failed logins or MFA challenges followed by a success from the same address, privileged sign-ins from residential-proxy networks that geolocate near the user, logins with a backup code, and new passkey or device registrations. In administrator audit logs, Customer Takeout creation, user-list downloads, audit-log investigation queries and Alert Center batch deletions. In Drive and OAuth logs, download spikes, external sharing to free mail providers, and authorisations of broad mail scopes to unapproved clients such as Thunderbird or Proton (GTIG, 2026-11-17). After a compromise, password changes alone are insufficient: revoke all sessions, refresh tokens and third-party OAuth permissions and remove unauthorised passkeys, backup codes and MFA devices (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

Triage: a directory export, a Customer Takeout or a passkey or device enrolment by an administrator can be routine; the cues in GTIG's account are an unfamiliar device, a non-corporate or residential-proxy network, or an enrolment right after an MFA-fatigue pattern (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

Defender takeaway
Move administrators and exposed staff to FIDO2 or WebAuthn hardware keys, which GTIG says cannot be approved through fatigue or intercepted by reverse proxies, require existing-administrator or out-of-band approval for new MFA devices and passkeys, and write session and OAuth revocation into compromise playbooks (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

item.title: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
item.description: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 fix CVE-2026-114938, an out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder that Calif, its discoverer, scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and says it turned into pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; Oracle scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity. Only x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI are affected, a trigger proof of concept is public, Calif withholds its product chains, a second researcher claims a working exploit with no release stated, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts without a confirmed success against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working exploit is available to its customers. NCSC.ch and BACS warn operators to update internet-reachable Java applications and identity services first, and Cisco's advisory, at version 1.3, lists Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not affected while Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual with no fix yet.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-114938updatedNATOA2

Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later and Oracle Java SE on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI: a heap overflow in the Base64 decoder that its discoverer chains into pre-authentication code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; fixed in 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts, none confirmed successful against its sensors (CVSS 3.1 8.1)

Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 list CVE-2026-114938 in the hotspot compiler component, which Oracle rates CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity (Oracle, 2026-11-17; OpenJDK, 2026-11-17). Calif, which found it, says HotSpot's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic, which uses AVX-512 VBMI instructions, calculates a negative output length for a short padded input and that length becomes a full 64-byte write that sends 62 bytes past the end of the array; only the landing position of the write is controllable, a misplaced write can crash the JVM (Calif, 2026-11-17). It scores the flaw CVSS 4.0 9.2 and reports pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, authenticated execution in several further server products, and a client-side path in which a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server is compromised (Calif, 2026-11-17). Tenable relays Immersive's claim of a working exploit with no release stated (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

The flaw needs an x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI and affects OpenJDK from 17.0.6 on, ARM64 hosts are not affected (Calif, 2026-11-17). CISA published an alert to patch immediately (CISA, 2026-11-17), and the NCSC.ch Cyber Security Hub says the published research demonstrates exploitation without establishing malicious exploitation (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-17); Talos has seen no exploitation in the wild yet and expects probing (Talos, 2026-11-18), while Tenable relays GreyNoise's report of exploitation attempts as of 2026-11-18, none confirmed successful against its sensors, and VulnCheck's statement that a working RCE exploit is available to its customers (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
A Java 17, 21, 25 or 27 runtime, or the Java 8 performance build, at or below the affected builds (Oracle, 2026-11-17), BACS says to check that the running applications actually use the corrected Java version (BACS, 2026-11-18). The CPU must report the avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi and bmi2 flags, which means Intel Ice Lake to Granite Rapids and AMD Zen 4 or newer (Upwind, 2026-11-17). Pre-authentication reach depends on the application decoding attacker-controlled Base64 with the basic or URL decoder of java.util.Base64 before it authenticates the caller (Upwind, 2026-11-17). Cisco's advisory (version 1.3) lists Secure Network Analytics and Secure Workload as affected and Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not (Cisco, 2026-11-20); Fortinet lists FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiWeb and others as not impacted, dozens of products as under investigation and none as affected (Fortinet, 2026-11-18); BACS adds internal systems and supplier-run Java software, banking software among it (translated from German) (BACS, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Unexplained hs_err_pid crash logs on internet-facing Java applications, where the log may not name Base64 because the crash comes later (Equixly, 2026-11-17); child processes of the server and administrative activity on identity, build and artifact platforms follow from Calif's chains. In request and application logs, Upwind suggests Base64-alphabet tokens of 32 or more characters that end in = with a length not a multiple of 4, starting with Authorization headers, and bursts of IllegalArgumentException from java.util.Base64$Decoder or of restarts (Upwind, 2026-11-17). An update does not remove a compromise that has already happened (BACS, 2026-11-18).
Defender takeaway
Update and restart, internet-reachable and identity services first. Where an update waits, Calif gives two JVM options, -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, which disables the hardware-accelerated Base64 path, or -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 hosts only, because OpenJDK on ARM does not recognize it and fails to start (Calif, 2026-11-17).
Update19 Nov 2026 05:03 UTCrun 2026-11-19T0355Z-intelaffected_productsbodycvesevidencesourcessummaryheadlinesourcing_notetitleentities

Cisco's product impact, published 2026-11-18, is at version 1.3: Secure Network Analytics, Secure Workload and further products are affected, Catalyst Center, IOS XE, ISE and UCS Central are not affected, Cisco offers no workaround, and its PSIRT is aware of proof-of-concept code but not of malicious use (Cisco, 2026-11-20). Fortinet says it is investigating the impact on its products and lists none as affected (Fortinet, 2026-11-18). Tenable relays GreyNoise's report of exploitation attempts as of 2026-11-18, none confirmed successful against its sensors, and VulnCheck's statement that a working RCE exploit is available to its customers (Tenable, 2026-11-17). BACS's warning of 2026-11-18 asks operators to prioritise internet-reachable applications and central sign-in services, to include internal systems, to clarify other Java software such as banking software with their suppliers and to have externally operated services confirm the fix, and says an update removes no compromise that has already happened (translated from German) (BACS, 2026-11-18). Tenable adds that as of 2026-11-18 Red Hat and Ubuntu had released no fix and Debian had fixed only its unstable branch, so hosts on those distributions had no stable vendor build yet, and that the Keycloak project recommended starting its server with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as an interim mitigation, its x86-64 container images tagged 26.8.2-1 and 26.8.2-2 carrying an affected Java build (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

Update20 Nov 2026 05:12 UTCrun 2026-11-20T0356Z-intelentitiesaffected_productssourcesbodysummarycves

Three more vendors published product status. Elastic says Elasticsearch 7.17.3 and later is affected with mitigating factors: remote code execution needs an authenticated user with at least read access on an affected CPU architecture, while unauthenticated actors can cause denial of service; Logstash 8.6.2 and later is affected only through the elastic_integration filter when an ingest pipeline decodes Base64 from an untrusted source, with a crash as the result, and Kibana, Beats, Elastic Agent, APM Server, the ECK operator and Elastic Maps Server are not affected, while Elasticsearch clusters that ECK manages follow the Elasticsearch rule (Elastic, 2026-11-19). Elastic plans fixes in 8.19.26, 9.4.10, 9.5.7 and 9.6.0 with a bundled JDK 27.0.1.1+4 and gives no dates, hot-fixed Elastic Cloud Serverless on 2026-11-18, and says fewer than about 5% of Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, on Azure only, run an affected CPU architecture; a self-managed node is affected only on an x86-64 CPU with AVX512_VBMI (Elastic, 2026-11-19).

Broadcom's Tanzu advisory TNZ-2026-1107 says several Tanzu products ship affected Java runtimes and lists released fixes: Java Buildpack 5.5.0 and 5.5.1, Ruby Buildpack 1.10.104, Tanzu OpenJDK 17.0.21.1+5, 21.0.13.1+5 and 25.0.5.1+5 and Foundation Core 3.1.19, 3.3.10 and 11.0.3, where the identity service and CredHub carry an affected Java 25 runtime that Tanzu has not yet confirmed from the bill of materials; it names -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as the preferred workaround (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). Palo Alto Networks lists fixed builds of Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector and the Secure Access HTML5 Gateway, says PAN-OS is not affected, offers no workaround and is not aware of any malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-20). None of these statuses changes the exploitation picture above.

Cisco's advisory is now at version 1.3 (2026-11-20), whose change log reads "Changed Catalyst Center from affected to not affected", and its product table shows Catalyst Center, IOS XE, ISE and UCS Central as not affected, so the Cisco product list above follows that version (Cisco, 2026-11-20). Siemens has published two advisories for CVE-2026-114938 and lists no fix for either: Siveillance Control and Siveillance Control Pro, the physical-security management systems, with the JVM option -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics on the client until Java is updated (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-19), and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual, where Siemens' immediate measure is to block direct internet access or shut the instances down (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-18). Neither Cisco nor Siemens reports exploitation of its products.

item.title: Puppet Enterprise report-deserialization RCE is on CISA KEV; upgrade to 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-17 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. A client holding any CA-signed agent certificate can run code on a Puppet Enterprise server as its service user by sending a crafted report, and where the CA autosigns requests without strong verification an unauthenticated attacker can first obtain that certificate; a trigger event has been public since 2026-11-03, and Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1 carry the fix. The same advisory fixed CVE-2026-115732, a certificate-name authorization bypass (CVSS 4.0 9.0) that lets a certificate for a name extending a real host name authenticate as that host; CISA lists only CVE-2026-115731.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-115731 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-115731, Puppet Enterprise before 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1: deserialization of a crafted agent report gives code execution as the Puppet service user to any holder of a CA-signed agent certificate, and unauthenticated where the CA autosigns; CISA lists it as exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.4)

CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-17 on evidence of active exploitation, naming no actor or victim (CISA, 2026-11-17). The flaw sits in Puppet's report-processing code as used by Puppet Server: a client that holds any CA-signed agent certificate can run arbitrary code on the server as its service user by sending a report with a crafted rich-data type in a PUT request, and where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification an unauthenticated network attacker can first obtain such a certificate (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03). The CNA scores it CVSS 4.0 9.4 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03) and Red Hat CVSS 3.1 9.9 (Red Hat, 2026-11-03).

The discoverers at Neodyme call the bug authenticated in the strict sense, because it needs a valid agent certificate, and say it allows code execution on the management server in a default configuration (Neodyme, 2026-11-03). The OpenVox advisory of the same day includes a full trigger event and says autosign is common in enterprise deployments and that code execution as the puppet user gives access to the CA signing key (OpenVox, 2026-11-03). Puppet's 2026.0.1 release notes list the flaw among the fixes in Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1 (Puppet, 2026-11-12), and the EUVD record names 2025.12.1 and 2023.8.13 as the fixed releases of the other two lines (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03); OpenVox fixes it in server 9.2.0 and 8.18.0 (oss-security, 2026-11-03), and Vox Pupuli says open-source Puppet will not receive any more updates (Vox Pupuli, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
A Puppet Enterprise or OpenVox server below the fixed releases that accepts agent connections; the reachable condition is a CA-signed agent certificate, which an outsider obtains where the CA autosigns without strong verification, a setup the OpenVox advisory calls common in enterprise deployments (OpenVox, 2026-11-03).
Detection
On the Puppet server, PUT requests to the agent report endpoint from hosts that enrolled recently, newly signed certificate requests that nobody approved, and child processes of the server's service account. A server that untrusted clients could reach before the upgrade should be treated as having exposed its CA signing key, since code execution as the puppet user reaches it (OpenVox, 2026-11-03), and the upgrade does not undo a key that was copied.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade now and, until then, avoid autosigning certificate requests without strong verification (Red Hat, 2026-11-03). The 2026.0.1 upgrade changes auth.conf wildcard matching, so a rule for *.example.com no longer matches example.com itself and rules that relied on that need review (Puppet, 2026-11-12).

The same Perforce advisory fixed a second flaw, CVE-2026-115732, an authorization bypass in the certificate-name matching of Puppet's authorization library, scored CVSS 4.0 9.0: a CA-signed certificate whose name extends or shortens an authorised host name is authorised as that host (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03). Neodyme's example is that an attacker who got a certificate for evil.target.lab.local can authenticate as target.lab.local, then fetch that host's catalog, which can carry configuration files with database credentials and API tokens, push spoofed facts and add exported resources (Neodyme, 2026-11-03). Where the CA autosigns, such a certificate can be requested for a name that does not exist yet, and OpenVox says autosign is not the default but is common in real deployments (OpenVox, 2026-11-03); NCSC.ch adds that in Puppet Enterprise the bypass also enables CA administration and remote command execution on managed nodes (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

The fix is in the same Puppet Enterprise builds, in Puppet Core 9.1.3 and 8.22.2 and, for OpenVox Server and OpenVoxDB, in 9.2.0 and 8.18.0 (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-18; OpenVox, 2026-11-03). CISA's catalog entry covers only CVE-2026-115731 (CISA, 2026-11-17); NCSC.ch labels the pair actively exploited with a proof of concept available and lists a community report as an additional source (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19), while the report The Hacker News quotes describes a CVE-2026-115731 intrusion, so exploitation of CVE-2026-115732 itself is not established (The Hacker News, 2026-11-18). NCSC.ch's temporary measures are to disable certificate autosigning, enforce strong request validation, audit the issued certificates for colliding names and review the CA configuration for signs of compromise (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

item.content:encoded:
Update18 Nov 2026 04:57 UTCrun 2026-11-18T0356Z-intelactionsbodyevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummary

Optimizely's own status entry says an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation to add the JavaScript to some customer projects, Report URI counts 178 organisations that served the code on 2026-11-16, and the Optimizely files carried the code from 2026-11-16 rather than 2026-11-13. The loader also hides in base64 where a host-name search misses it.

Optimizely says an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, that it has fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code, and that it secured affected user accounts; that post named no flaw class, CVE or count, and the status entry's later post of 2026-11-18 is described below (Optimizely, 2026-11-18). The status entry covers the Optimizely files only; how the Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly scripts were reached is still unknown.

Report URI's timeline adds that the card skimmer was added to the clipper at 13:43 UTC on 2026-11-16, that a mass clean-up ran between about 20:40 and 21:10 UTC, and that a snippet cleaned and then re-infected shows the writer still had access at that point (Report URI, 2026-11-16). Contradiction on dates: Ohey puts the change to the Optimizely project files at 2026-11-13 together with the Kissmetrics and StorifyMe scripts (Ohey, 2026-11-17), while Report URI's first Optimizely injection is at 04:21 UTC on 2026-11-16; Report URI's logged first-hand record is the better dated one, and the earlier Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly wave is not in the 178 (Report URI, 2026-11-16).

The injected loader came in three forms: a plain script tag, the same address hidden in base64 and decoded with atob(), which a search for the host name misses, and a full inline copy that runs through eval (Report URI, 2026-11-16). Cards entered in hosted payment iframes were out of the skimmer's reach, while cards typed into a site's own form fields were not (Report URI, 2026-11-16).

Open finding: OptimJack: poisoned scripts served by Optimizely, Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly route iPhones to exploit-kit stages, the Optimizely files also carry a crypto clipper and card skimmer, and the University of Basel site loaded a poisoned StorifyMe widget on 2026-11-14 →

item.title: Craft CMS unauthenticated SQL injection gives admin takeover; CCCS reports exploitation; update to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2
item.description: CVE-2026-123488 is an unauthenticated SQL injection in the front-end search of Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1 on MySQL and MariaDB that gives read and write access to the database, including setting the admin flag or overwriting password hashes. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security says open source reporting indicates exploitation in the wild and VulnCheck lists it in its own KEV database; no first-hand telemetry or CISA listing was found. Craft fixed it in 4.18.9 and 5.11.2 and offers a query-string block as a workaround.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-123488exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-123488, Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1: an unauthenticated SQL injection in front-end search lets a visitor become an administrator on MySQL and MariaDB; the Canadian Cyber Centre reports exploitation in the wild and 4.18.9 and 5.11.2 fix it (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

Craft CMS 4.0.0 before 4.18.9 and 5.0.0 before 5.11.2 contain an unauthenticated SQL injection in front-end search: the attribute parameter is concatenated into the query unsanitized and emulated PDO prepares allow stacked statements, so a remote attacker can read and write the database, setting the admin flag or overwriting password hashes in the users table to gain administrator access (CVSS 4.0 9.3) (VulnCheck, 2026-11-06). Craft's own advisory, published on 2026-10-22 as critical, places the flaw on the front end of any site that uses craft.search, says it affects only MySQL and MariaDB, and says the write primitive was used to set the admin flag on user ID 1 (Craft CMS, 2026-10-22). The fixed releases are 4.18.9 and 5.11.2, and Craft's temporary workaround is to block front-end requests that carry the bracketed attribute token, plain or encoded, in the query string (Craft CMS, 2026-10-22). ENISA's record for CVE-2026-123488 lists Craft's advisory among its references (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-06).

On exploitation, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security's update of 2026-11-12 says open source reporting indicates the flaw is exploited in the wild (CCCS, 2026-11-12), and VulnCheck's advisory page states that it is in the VulnCheck KEV database (VulnCheck, 2026-11-06). No first-hand telemetry, victim statement or CISA listing was found.

Exposure
Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1 on MySQL or MariaDB whose public pages use craft.search.
Detection
Web access logs for front-end search requests whose query string carries the bracketed attribute token that Craft's workaround blocks; database audit for changes to the admin column or password hashes in the users table, and new administrator accounts or sessions afterwards. Updating closes the injection but not an administrator flag or hash that was already written.
Defender takeaway
Update every Craft CMS site to the fixed release now, since the attack needs no account and ends in administrator access, and check the users table on any internet-facing site that ran an older build.
